01 / AN INVITATION

A letter to investors.

Download letter · PDF

October 11, 2026

Dear prospective investor,

I am building RegFire around twenty-six years of experience across registration, sales, marketing, onsite delivery, operations, and technology. I have stood in the shoes of the people who sell the event, build it, run it, and support it. That understanding of how the whole business fits together is the foundation of RegFire.

The intended launch scope runs from a birthday party for twenty people to a major trade show. One-time events are a core part of the business. We welcome them all day, every day. Repeat business is valuable, but our model is designed to make each event worthwhile on its own through easy setup, flexible software, and low delivery costs.

Great technology alone does not make a great registration business. If delivery requires too many people, departments, and handoffs, the margin can disappear. RegFire is being built to simplify the work for everyone involved, so organizers can move quickly and the business can retain more of the value it creates.

In my own experience, I can complete major trade-show registration setup, including integrations, in a couple of hours on my own where the work once involved seven or eight people across four departments. That is the operating insight behind RegFire: put the right knowledge into the workflow and remove unnecessary handoffs. It is my experience, not a guaranteed staffing ratio or setup time for every customer.

AI makes software easier to build. Knowing what to build, how the pieces connect, and what can go wrong at a live event still takes experience. I have worked through challenges across ticketed shows, major trade shows, lead retrieval, and session tracking. RegFire brings that perspective into the product from the start.

An investment in RegFire is also an investment in my judgment and ability to execute. The goal is a system that works for sales, marketing, technology, operations, and the people onsite, without making every event a custom project. The working product provides a foundation; dependable end-to-end delivery and event-level margins remain the measures we will use to prove the business.

The accompanying film and business plan explain that vision and the work ahead. Financial scenarios are planning assumptions, and financing terms will be discussed separately. If you see the opportunity in combining practical expertise with a simpler way to run registration, I would welcome a conversation.

Mike Blazejewski
RegFire
blaze@regfire.events
